Handling errors in forms

Draft not synced yet.

Every form talks to a server, and every server fails now and then. When it does, the person filling in the form should keep what they typed, learn what happened in plain words, and know what to do next. A message that only says "Something went wrong" tells them none of that, so name the field, the reason, and the way out.

Say which field

Put the error next to the field it belongs to, in the same colour as the field's border, and move the focus there when the person submits. A summary at the top of the form helps on long forms: it lists each problem as a link to its field, so a keyboard or a screen reader reaches them in order.

Status codes

The server's answer decides the words. A validation error comes back with its field names; anything else is shown once, above the button, with a way to try again.

CodeWhat the person reads
422 UnprocessableThe fields to fix, each by its name
500 Internal Server ErrorSaving failed on our side; your answers are kept, try again
503 Service UnavailableWe are updating; try again in a minute

Keep what they typed

Never clear the form after an error. Keep every value, keep the scroll position, and keep the button enabled so the person can send it again once the reason is gone.
